title: Reusable Classes and Maintainable CSS
summary: Organize CSS around reusable patterns instead of copying nearly identical rules.

sketchBlocks.title: Give repeated content blocks one shared hook
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
The portfolio already has several `section` and `article` elements that look like cards, but they are styled by element type rather than by a reusable component name. A shared class lets the same visual pattern work across different semantic elements.

**Worked example:**

```html
<section class="card">
  ...
</section>
```

**Line by line:** `section` keeps its semantic meaning. `class="card"` adds a reusable CSS hook without changing the content or document structure.

tryItExercises.title: Give repeated content blocks one shared card hook
tryItExercises.prompt:
**Problem**

The same kind of reusable content block appears across Home, About, Projects, and Contact, but those existing `section` and `article` elements do not yet share one reusable class hook.

**Task**

Keep the existing semantic elements and their content. Add `class="card"` to the existing reusable content blocks in `index.html`, `about.html`, `projects/portfolio.html`, and `contact.html`. Do not add wrappers and do not style `.card` yet.
tryItExercises.hint: Add the same `card` class to the existing reusable section/article blocks across the four HTML pages; leave styles.css unchanged.

help.concept: A reusable CSS component starts with one shared class hook on the existing semantic elements that represent the same UI pattern.
help.hint_2: Apply that hook consistently in index.html, about.html, projects/portfolio.html, and contact.html.

tryItExercises.title: Give every reusable card shared inner spacing
tryItExercises.prompt:
**Problem**

The reusable content blocks now share the `.card` hook, but the class does not yet provide a common component style.

**Task**

Keep the new card classes in all four HTML pages. In `styles.css`, add `.card { padding: var(--space-section); }` so every reusable card gets the same shared inner spacing.
tryItExercises.hint: Style the existing `.card` hook once with the shared section-spacing token.

help.concept: Once repeated elements share a class, one CSS rule can style the component consistently everywhere.

tryItExercises.title: Give every card the same surface
tryItExercises.prompt:
## CSS task

The reusable card hooks are working, but the blocks still blend into the page `background`. Because they all share the `.card` class now, you can fix that visual problem once instead of styling `section` and `article` separately. Add a later `.card` rule with `background-color: #fff;`. Check Home, About, Projects, and Contact: every card should pick up the same clean white surface.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on.
tryItExercises.hint: Extend the reusable component with a later `.card` rule instead of writing separate element-specific rules.

help.concept: A shared class makes one component-level change propagate across different pages and semantic elements.
help.hint_2: Preview more than one page to verify the same component style is reused.

sketchBlocks.title: Polish the component without changing its HTML

tryItExercises.title: Polish the reusable card boundary
tryItExercises.prompt:
## CSS task

The cards now read as separate surfaces, but their edges still feel a little rigid and inconsistent with the rest of the polished site. Refine the component itself rather than editing individual pages: add a later `.card` rule with `border-radius: 0.75rem;` and `border-color: #e2e8f0;`. The preview should show the same softer card treatment wherever the reusable class appears.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on.
tryItExercises.hint: Keep the existing `.card` styles and add the radius and `border`-`color` as another cumulative component refinement.

help.concept: Reusable component classes keep visual refinements consistent across every instance of the pattern.
help.hint_1: Use one `.card` rule for both declarations.
help.hint_2: Do not change the HTML hooks again; the class should already be present from the first step.

quizDraft.title: Choose a reusable selector
quizDraft.prompt: Which selector is designed to be reused on multiple elements that share the same visual pattern?
quizDraft.hint: Compare the choices by whether they reduce duplicated styling and reuse an existing styling role.

help.concept: Maintainable CSS keeps repeated presentation decisions in reusable selectors and shared values.
help.hint_1: Prefer choices that let one styling decision serve repeated content without unnecessary duplication.
help.hint_2: Reject choices that require unrelated markup changes or repeat the same literal styling in many places.

quizDraft.title: Build a reusable class
quizDraft.prompt: Put the rule pieces in valid order.
quizDraft.hint: Open the class rule, place declarations inside it, then close the rule.

help.concept: A reusable class uses the same rule syntax as other selectors.
help.hint_1: Open the class rule, place declarations inside it, then close the rule.
help.hint_2: Keep the cumulative site intact and make only the focused change required by this exercise.

quizDraft.title: Select a class
quizDraft.hint: The blank belongs in the selector. Choose the option that targets an existing reusable class rather than an element or id.

help.concept: Reusable class selectors let the same styling role apply to multiple elements without duplicating page-specific rules.
help.hint_1: Look for the selector form used for a class hook that already exists in the HTML.
help.hint_2: The completed selector should match the shared card role rather than one specific tag.

quizDraft.title: Reuse a spacing value
quizDraft.prompt: Choose the expression that consumes the existing reusable spacing value.
quizDraft.hint: The blank should consume a spacing value that already belongs to the shared design system.

help.concept: A maintainable rule reuses an existing spacing token instead of introducing another literal measurement.
help.hint_1: Choose the option that points back to the previously declared shared spacing decision.
help.hint_2: The completed declaration should keep card spacing controlled from one shared source.
